items.label: Iron Mountain Goldman Sachs conference 2026 (09-08-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CFO on Asset Lifecycle Management: ALM did '$30 million of revenue' in 2021

set.signal: CFO on Asset Lifecycle Management: 'in 2021, I think we did $30 million of revenue'; 'This year we projected we do approximately $1 billion'. The ALM TAM is '$35 billion estimated', 75% of it corporate clients. In hyperscale data center decommissioning, memory 'might be 50% or more' of the value of decommissioned gear; some memory SKUs have been 'up as much as 30%' and others down, and Q2 carried relatively more DDR3 versus more DDR4 in Q1; memory pricing has been 'stable to even slightly up' since the end of Q2. Hyperscale decommissioning is a revenue share model where Iron Mountain 'might get 20%' of the gear's sale price, with margins 'low double digit to high teens'; enterprise ALM is fee for service with margins 'mid-20s to 30s'.

items.reason: Hedge kept: the CFO said 'I think' about the 2021 ALM revenue figure; the signal had dropped it.
items.evidence: In the ALM business, which is a business that in 2021, I think we did $30 million of revenue. This year we projected we do approximately $1 billion.
